source_checks.finding: Page section 'To help protect yourself from phishing scams:' lists 'Don't click links or download attachments in unexpected messages.' (verified exact words). It also says: 'If you think the message could be legit, contact the company or bank using a phone number, email, or website you know is real.' Applies to any device and unexpected messages, which matches the user's bank message.

Page says: 'Scammers pretend to be someone they're not, like a representative from a well-known company or the government' and 'They also create fake websites and encrypt them to make you think they're safe when they're not.' (verified, with the page's curly apostrophes). The passage's wording is supported. The target uses only the first part, which is accurate.

Page says: 'make sure your security software, operating system, and internet browser are up to date.' 'Update your phone's operating system, too.' and 'And turn on automatic updates to keep up with the latest protections.' (verified). The passage's wording is supported. Applies to any device.
Page says: 'Report scammers to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.' (verified exact words). Applies to any device and any scam.

required_actions.action: Do not click links in the unexpected bank message
Contact the bank using a phone number, email, or website the user knows is real, if the message could be legitimate
Keep security software, operating system, and internet browser up to date
Report the scammer to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Be aware that scammers pretend to be a bank or other trusted company
